fixture-good-prompt.notes: Existing goodPrompt fixture. Well-headed structure — trivial for section detection, a baseline for false positives on the harder findings.

two-agent-defs.notes: Reconstruction of the failure mode: two distinct agent definitions clustered by v1 as duplicates because they share the 'agent' vocabulary. Regression fence — every pipeline MUST label this as related-not-duplicate.

texts: The code review agent is an experienced senior engineer that reviews pull requests.
The refactor agent is an experienced senior engineer that proposes structural improvements to code.
relatedNotDuplicate.note: Two distinct agent definitions. Share 'experienced senior engineer' phrasing but describe different agents with different scopes.

anthropic-style-reviewer.notes: Anthropic conventions: XML tags for structural sections, <thinking> block for reasoning directives, <examples> block for few-shot. Representative of Claude prompts. Simple example inside <examples> tests that the classifier doesn't confuse example content with a rule.

openai-style-support.notes: OpenAI conventions: markdown headings, terse imperative instructions, safety block at the end, tool-use hints as inline bullets. Representative of ChatGPT-style system prompts.

gemini-style-analyst.notes: Gemini conventions: explicit reasoning-directive section, verbose step-by-step guidance, chain-of-thought made mandatory in output. contradictions.note: Subtle contradiction inside Guardrails — 'thorough' pulls one way, 'concise' the other, both marked 'always'/'where you can'. Realistic instance of the kind of contradiction that slips through review.

cline-inspired-coding-agent.notes: Open-source coding-agent style (inspired by Cline / Continue / Aider). Model-agnostic. Has role + workflow + tool-rules + editing-conventions + safety. Tests classifier on 'workflow' as a task-family label and 'tool use rules' as constraints.

unheaded-wall.notes: Wall-of-text prompt with no headings — stresses semantic chunking. Contains explicit duplicates ('Always be polite' / 'Please always be polite' / 'Be concise' + 'Always be polite'), demonstrates unheaded canonical sections (role, task, constraints, output all present but unlabelled).
